items.title: Stanley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I think I heard that — with Lester Young on it? [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, it’s quite recent.

ctx.x: In 1935 I joined the Royal Observer Corps. And I was in that until 1945. It was attached to the RAF. We were — there was immense air traffic in England after the Battle of Britain. We joined the Royal Observer Corps because we thought we could get out of the infantry and go into it, but we were stuck where we were. We had radio equipment and the light anti-aircraft, but our main job was positioning. It had been German planes, but the hedge hopping defeated radar. The radar was fine when they were up a bit, but if…
I think I heard that — with Lester Young on it?

Yeah, it’s quite recent. Well that was different you know. This is a different audience and element. I mean you’d go to the Savoy Ballroom or places like that, there would be applause. But it wasn’t hysterical in the way it seemed to me. But fortunately, we turned to Ellington. He did a concert while I was there, it was the “Deep South Suite,” and that sort of confirmed to me that the battle wasn’t lost. So after that we agreed to be married, and Helen came to England and we lived there about twelve years.
